# Application Index Ingestion Performance and Slow Operations

Use this skill when the target index is experiencing write or query performance problems:

- Bulk or write requests are being rejected on this index
- High `index_failed` count in monitoring
- Slow search queries against this index
- Slow indexing operations (bulk taking longer than expected)
- Circuit-breaker trips associated with queries on this index (fielddata, request, in-flight)

## Workflow

1. Use `app-index-triage-index_indexing_failures` to check the monitoring stream for non-zero `index_failed` counts — shows when failures started and how many occurred per bucket.
2. Use `app-index-triage-index_write_rejections` to find rejection log entries in the server log scoped to this index.
3. Use `app-index-triage-slow_index_log` for p95/p99 slow-log latency. An empty result means either slow-log thresholds are not configured, or all operations are within threshold — call this out explicitly.
4. Use `app-index-triage-circuit_breaker_trips` if queries are failing with out-of-memory or fielddata errors.

## Output guidance

- Distinguish between indexing failures (mapper/mapping errors → use mapping skill) and rejections (thread-pool pressure → escalate to cluster resource skill if node-wide).
- Report slow-log p95 and p99 in milliseconds — note whether the logger is `index.search.slowlog` or `index.indexing.slowlog`.
- If circuit breakers are tripping, identify the type: `fielddata` (text field agg/sort without `fielddata:true`) vs `request` (large agg against this index) vs `in_flight_requests`.
- Note if the index_failed rate correlates with a time window visible in the indexing failures chart.
description: Investigate bulk rejections, indexing failures, slow search/indexing operations, and circuit-breaker trips for the target index.
name: Application Index Ingestion Performance and Slow Operations
